newsitem.title: DENMARK: Final ruling on Danish EU case now seen in April.
newsitem.headline: Final ruling on Danish EU case now seen in April.

text.p: Danish Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen expects a final Supreme Court ruling on the legality of Denmark's European Union membership in mid-April 1998, a government source told Reuters on Monday.

If, as expected, the court rejects on appeal a suit by a group of Danes claiming that aspects of Denmark's EU membership are unconstitutional, there will be a referendum on last June's Amsterdam amendments to the EU treaty in May, the source added.
He said the court was expected to finish hearing the appeal on March 24 and it would take a further two weeks for judges to vote on the case and write the judgement.

Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen said last week that the referendum would be some time after mid-March 1998 and that the government would propose a firm date after parliament reconvenes from its summer recess, in October 1997.

On June 27 the Danish High Court dismissed a suit by the group, which charged that since joining the EU in 1973 Denmark had ceded national authority to European institutions in breach of its own constitution.
Most analysts expect the appeal to fail, but if it succeeds the government must either renegotiate all its EU treaties or amend the constitution, both long and tortuous processes.

The centre-left coalition government believes its case is watertight and lawyers from both sides say the state attorneys' task has been eased by rulings that the case should be limited to events since the 1992 Maastricht Treaty.
Danes, traditionally cool toward European integration, rejected the treaty outright in a 1992 referendum.
Voters grudgingly approved the treaty the following year on condition that Denmark opt out of economic and monetary union and joint defence, policing and asylum policies.
